papers.title_in_file: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
papers.version_note: arXiv:2610.10629v1 [cs.AI], 7 Oct 2026; the text is the record's paper. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
papers.what_it_is: A position paper with a simulation study measuring an admission gate that confines LLM-agent self-evolution to the runtime harness in a synthetic credit-screening pipeline, with an EU AI Act mapping.

existing.note: The numbers are right. Section 10 limits the claim: the held-out history (Hval) is an interleaved half of the same pre-shift stream, labelled by the same deterministic rule as the gate pool, so zero false admissions is expected for any gated arm. The informative contrast is against the no-gate arm and on the post-shift held-out window. Section 7.1 also limits the no-gate harm: under the threshold family the no-gate arm's missed-flag rate stays near the oracle's; the loosening is a scope and structural effect.
existing.value: The authors report that the gated dual loop admitted 144 of 7,449 candidate changes, none of which worsened error on held-out history, and that the no-gate arm admitted 309 harmful changes and left missed flags above 10% in 49 of 90 runs; the authors state that the false-admission audit is weak by construction, because the gate half and the audit half are interleaved halves of the same pre-shift stream labelled by the same deterministic rule.
quotes: the gated dual loop admitted 144 of 7,449 candidate changes, none of which worsened error on held-out history
the same loops admitted 309 harmful changes and left missed flags above 10% in 49 of 90 runs
The false-admission audit is weak by construction.
Hsel and Hval are interleaved halves of the same pre-shift stream labelled by the same deterministic rule
existing.certainty_reason: Started LOW: an empirical result from one synthetic study. Not upgraded.
existing.reader_inference: The held-out history that the 144 admissions are checked against is the same pre-shift stream the gate used, so the zero is close to guaranteed. The 49 of 90 comparison is the informative result.

assertions.value: The authors argue that the runtime harness is the only legitimate mutable surface for self-evolution in a regulated credit pipeline, because it is the auditable one: weights cannot be diffed into named changes and a harness can.
quotes: the runtime harness is the only legitimate mutable surface, because it is the auditable one
Weights cannot be diffed into named changes; a harness can.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's position argument; no experiment in the paper tests it against a weight-update alternative.

assertions.value: The authors state that the engine may rewrite instruction text, tool-call logic and primitive composition, may not fine-tune, and that the served model is pinned by digest; they state this is a design commitment and that no model is pinned in the simulation.

(a design commitment: no model is pinned in our simulation)

assertions.value: The authors report that all 540 of the 540 gate logs written in their experiments, 43,814 records in all, verify under the hash chain.

assertions.value: The authors define the admission rule: a candidate harness is admitted only if the 95% lower bound of the paired reduction in errors of the relevant kind on the gate half of the retrospective pool is above zero, and the share of cases the deployed harness answers correctly that the candidate turns wrong is at most ε = 0.005.
quotes: paired 95% lower bound of reduction > 0; ε = 0.005
The candidate is admitted iff
The tolerance ε = 0.005 is not zero because execution noise makes strict non-regression unsatisfiable

assertions.value: The authors state that admission is a write and not only a decision: before a candidate reaches the runtime the gate appends a record (including the digests of the deployed and candidate harness, the counts behind the decision and the decision itself), and rejections are written with the same schema.
quotes: Admission is a write, not only a decision. Before a candidate reaches the runtime the gate appends
Rejections are written with the same schema.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its record schema in Section 5.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that operational feedback arrives in windows of 500 cases, that every flagged case is reviewed by an analyst so its false positive becomes visible, and that cleared cases are audited at 5%, so most misses stay invisible; they call this asymmetry deliberate and realistic.

Every flagged case is reviewed by an analyst, so its false positive becomes visible; cleared cases are audited at 5%, so most misses stay invisible.
This asymmetry is deliberate and realistic

assertions.value: The authors state that the local loop may change one parameter or one clause of the deployed primitive per candidate, that the global loop may replace the primitive with another from a typed library (here a check on the first-layer stake against a check on the effective stake along the ownership chain), and that the global loop has no privileged path to deployment because the same gate applies.
quotes: The local loop (Algorithm 1) may change one parameter or one clause of the deployed primitive per candidate.
The global loop (Algorithm 2) may replace the primitive with another from a typed library
a check on the stake held through the first-layer vehicle versus a check on the effective stake along the ownership chain
path to deployment: the same gate applies.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own engine in Section 5.2.

assertions.value: The authors define ground truth as a versioned rule: before T flag when the hit type is in scope and the stake held through the first-layer vehicle is at least 25%; from T one of three re-interpretations applies: a threshold rise to 30, 40 or 50%, a narrowing of the qualifying hit types, or a threshold on the effective stake with multi-layer chains in 30, 50 or 70% of cases.
quotes: Before T (rule v1): flag when the hit type is in scope and the stake held through the first-layer vehicle is at least 25%.
the ownership threshold rises to 30, 40 or 50%
with multi-layer chains in 30, 50 or 70% of cases.
No threshold or scope edit to the first-layer check can express this rule.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its three shift families in Section 6.1.

assertions.value: The authors state the experimental design: a stream of 23,000 screening alerts with the shift at T = 70%, adaptation on [T, 85%), held-out evaluation on [85%, 100%] (3,450 alerts per run), and 10 seeds per cell over 3 families × 3 severities = 9 cells, 90 runs.
quotes: 23,000 screening alerts; shift at T = 70%; adaptation on [T, 85%); held-out evaluation on [85%, 100%]
The held-out window holds 3,450 alerts per run
10 per cell; 3 families × 3 severities = 9 cells, 90 runs

assertions.value: The authors state that at T the retrospective pool is relabelled by applying rule v2 to the stored case facts, which makes the adaptation supervised at the level of the rule and autonomous at the level of the harness, and that a mis-encoded rule would be faithfully optimised towards.

the adaptation is supervised at the level of the rule and autonomous at the level of the harness
a mis-encoded rule would be faithfully optimised towards

assertions.value: The authors report that in the high-severity structural cell the dual loop recovered in 5/10 seeds at ε = 0.005, rejecting the exactly correct harness 24 times, with a mean false-positive rate of 18.1%, and that doubling the tolerance to ε = 0.010, tested on the structural family only, recovers 10/10 seeds without any false admission.

assertions.value: The authors state that no harmful change was admitted at either tolerance value, so the protective side of the trade-off between regression guarding and rejecting correct changes is not measured by this track.

assertions.value: The authors state that a fixed ε conflates noise with regression and that a tolerance scaled to the expected noise on the cases a candidate changes would separate them and is the next revision of the rule; until then ε is a policy parameter.

assertions.value: The authors report that the harness's rendered text ranged from 151 to 253 characters across all runs, and that the gated dual loop made at most 4 admissions in a run against up to 13 for the no-gate arm.

assertions.value: The authors argue that a harness-only engine with a fixed edit space, a fixed library and a fixed admission rule is a way of making change pre-determinable under the EU AI Act provision on pre-determined changes, because the reachable harnesses and the admitting rule can be written into the technical documentation before deployment.
